target_3_burn_conversion_gate_verdict.the_mechanism_behind_the_refutation_whic: The gate's CDD-ADD LIMB IS A CONSTANT, AND A CONSTANT CANNOT GATE. Measured across every day of G22 and G23 on the same S110-grafted ladder (n=20): d_gw_cdd at horizon 1 is POSITIVE 20/20 (min +0.129, max +2.256); the near limb h0+h1 is positive 19/20 (min -0.357, max +2.073, median +1.115). The near-horizon CDD run-delta never changes sign - it is a model-cycle artifact (each successive run raises the D+1 CDD as the target resolves), not a demand signal. So the gate, fed the near horizons, licenses an up-lean EVERY SINGLE DAY and can never decline. days.cross_cutting_mbo_finding: THE EIA THURSDAY IS HALF BUILT BEFORE THE PRINT, AND THE FIRST SIXTY SECONDS AFTER IT DECIDE WHETHER THAT HALF SURVIVES. Across all fourteen EIA Thursdays in g17-g23, the pre-print window's share of the day's absolute travel has median 49.5% (IQR ~34-59%) - the window is not a coil, it is half the session, and on my day it held the session high fifty-four seconds before the release. What the print supplies is not a direction but an ARBITER function, and it is measurable in the tape's first minute. On the six Thursdays that entered 10:30 with a chain-sided UP run of at least +300, the sixty-second impulse separates the outcomes without a single exception across five groups: an impulse inside +/-300 and the run continues (0416 +720, 0430 +1230, 0528 +2100, 0604 +1130), an impulse at or beyond -300 and the run round-trips in full and closes negative (0625 -60, 0716 -20). The separation is clean at 30, 60 and 120 seconds and starts to fail at 300, which places the arbiter inside the first two minutes - exactly where the standing NYMEX-canary lag says the information is. Underneath that sits the block's real structural fact, which is not Thursday-specific at all: on this tape heavy BUY aggression does not deliver price and heavy SELL aggression is unremarkable. Same-day signed flow versus same-day price across all seventy sessions - buy >+1000 agrees 41%, >+1500 29%, >+2000 25%, >+3000 20%, monotone; sell over the identical thresholds flat at 46/43/46/47%. At >+3000, eight of the ten days closed down and six carry absorb_session=true. The same quantity measured one day EARLIER is a coin flip (4/9), which is how my blind came to treat 0715's +6,326 - the largest buy flow in seven groups - as its bullish evidence for a day that closed -20. It was reading a same-day bearish tell as a next-day bullish one.

clears_the_bar.statement: On an EIA Thursday that arrives at 10:29 carrying a chain-sided UP run of at least +300 from the prior close, the sixty seconds after 10:30 adjudicate the run. An impulse inside +/-300 confirms it and the day continues up; an impulse at or beyond -300 rejects it and the day round-trips the run in full and closes at or below flat. Do not carry a chain-sided sign THROUGH the print - carry it TO the print and let the first minute decide.
clears_the_bar.mechanism: The pre-print run is inventory, not conviction: it is built by desks positioning for the number. The print is the scheduled moment at which that inventory must be defended. A counter impulse means the inventory is being liquidated by the people who built it, which is why the round-trip overshoots rather than stopping at flat.
clears_the_bar.scope: Pre-print UP runs only. On the five Thursdays entering 10:29 with a run of -300 or worse, no sixty-second impulse reached |300| at all, so the rule has nothing to say there and must not be applied symmetrically.
clears_the_bar.falsifier: A pre-print-UP Thursday whose sixty-second impulse is at or beyond -300 and which still closes materially up, or one whose impulse stays inside +/-150 and which nonetheless round-trips.
clears_the_bar.forward_test: G24+ EIA Thursdays. Two fires and four declines is thin, and the deflationary reading - that this is ordinary first-minute momentum - is not excluded by n=6.
